teaser.text: ResMed sells the equipment, supplies, software, and services that help people breathe and sleep at home. To understand its business, follow one dollar from a prescribed machine to the provider who buys it, the patient who uses it, and the costs ResMed pays to make the system work.

stock.title: ResMed Inc. stock forecast: 2027–2029 scenarios
stock.meta_description: ResMed's forecast weighs bear, base and bull outcomes against patient demand, cash generation, competition and Astral.
stock.opening: The weighted scenario is $249.58 in October 2027 and $286.46 in October 2029, with 25% bear, 60% base and 15% bull probabilities. It hinges on durable patient continuation and cash generation while ResMed defends share and resolves Astral.
stock.closing: The full ResMed Inc. memo also explains its business, rivals, management, and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could ResMed Inc.'s shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The probability-weighted price is $249.58 in October 2027, a 5% total return including dividends. It reaches $272.52 in October 2028, a 16% return. By October 2029, the weighted price is $286.46, a 23% return. The three-year range runs from $186.18 in the bear case to $454.58 in the bull case, against today’s $239.77.
The final scenario probabilities are 25% bear, 60% base and 15% bull.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for ResMed Inc., and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The bear case lowers earnings to $1,619 million in the first window and $1,636 million in the second. It reaches $1,657 million in the third. Philips may regain share, Astral remains suspended, MatrixCare leaves the portfolio and GLP-1 treatment or provider capacity may slow starts and resupply. The bull case reaches $1,829 million, then $1,999 million and $2,178 million as home testing, virtual care, adherence and manufacturing efficiency exceed the base path.

blocks.heading: How much cash does ResMed Inc. really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow starts with cash from operations and subtracts purchases of property, plant and equipment. In FY2026, free cash flow exceeded net income, which supports the quality of reported earnings. It nevertheless fell slightly from FY2025 because capital spending increased and more cash moved into operating needs.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay today for ResMed Inc.?

paragraphs.text: P/E compares the share price with earnings per share. A trailing P/E uses the last twelve months of profit; a forward P/E uses an estimate of future profit. ResMed’s FY2026 diluted GAAP EPS was lower than management’s adjusted, non-GAAP EPS because the adjusted measure excluded selected items such as acquired-asset amortization and restructuring costs. That adjustment can clarify ongoing operations, but only if the excluded costs are genuinely unusual.

dividend.closing: The full memo also explains ResMed Inc.’s business, rivals, management choices and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does ResMed Inc. pay in dividends per share?

paragraphs.text: On August 6, ResMed set out approximately $1.5 billion of repurchases and raised the quarterly dividend to $0.66. Later that month, it signed a $450 million accelerated share repurchase with Citibank, funded partly by MatrixCare proceeds and cash on hand. The bank delivered an initial block of shares, with final settlement scheduled for December 2026. A lower average share price would produce more shares, and a higher one fewer.

blocks.heading: What could change ResMed Inc.’s dividend?

paragraphs.text: Dividends start from the $0.66 quarterly rate. The bear case holds the annual dividend at $2.64 because the board may pause increases. The base case assumes another 10% annual increase, producing $2.706, $2.9844 and $3.28284 across the three windows. The bull case assumes 12% increases, producing $2.7192, $3.045504 and $3.41096448. The base path follows five years of increases and the latest 10% raise, while the bear path allows for Astral, portfolio and cash demands.

blocks.heading: What has ResMed Inc. guided for fiscal 2027?

paragraphs.text: For the year ending June 2027, ResMed forecasts revenue of $5.75 billion–$5.85 billion. It forecasts non-GAAP earnings per share of $12.00–$12.25, representing growth of 7%–10%. Non-GAAP means management excludes selected accounting charges from its preferred performance measure.

blocks.heading: Has ResMed Inc. kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: ResMed also kept one measurable promise. In April 2026, management reiterated a gross-margin outlook of 62–63%. FY26 non-GAAP gross margin was 62.4%, inside that range. On balance, equity pay creates genuine downside for executives, but the board should judge adjusted bonuses alongside reported profit, dilution and cash generation. That is the standard by which owners can decide whether ResMed’s leadership is truly on their side.

blocks.heading: What has ResMed Inc.'s revenue and profit trend been over the last eight quarters?

paragraphs.text: Revenue grew 8.6% from the June 2025 quarter, or approximately 8% at constant currency. The quarterly sequence shows continuing expansion rather than a sudden demand collapse, although the latest growth rate was slower than the preceding quarters.

blocks.heading: What should investors watch in ResMed Inc.'s next results?

paragraphs.text: The October 29, 2026 results call should show the first quarter of fiscal 2027 after the MatrixCare disposal, the enlarged repurchase program and the Noctrix acquisition. Compare headline sales with core sales, then compare cash generation with spending. Normal seasonal revenue movement and slightly lower year-over-year first-quarter gross margin would not, by themselves, disprove the annual plan.

Astral is the more serious operational risk because its component failure can interrupt life-sustaining treatment. A leaking supercapacitor can damage circuitry and stop ventilation, while replacement boards face supply constraints. The safety action covers 168,069 devices globally, and February 17, 2027 is the UK action deadline for healthcare organisations. That date does not promise worldwide repairs or a sales restart.
